object_description: two compact buildings of different heights enclosing a shared courtyard
design_condition: Two buildings are concentrated along Ansermet Square, preserving much of the park, while the underground gymnasium uses the topography to create a gradient toward the natural terrain.

positive.statement: The compact layout leaves most of the park free and supports pedagogical-functional suitability and flexibility.

position.rationale: Two compact masses and substantial surrounding open area are clearly visible across all views.

positive.statement: The classroom and special-room wing provides very good visual connections between the entrance zone, teachers’ area, foyer and playground.

position.rationale: The taller eastern wing is the most plausible classroom and special-room location.

positive.statement: Clustered classrooms, group rooms and checkrooms encourage varied uses and combinations while complying with fire-safety regulations.

position.rationale: Interior clusters are not distinguishable; the taller wing provides a useful approximation.

positive.statement: The vertical light halls create the desired centering and references between floors.

position.rationale: Light halls are interior; the upper portion of the taller wing is used as a surface proxy.

positive.statement: The building volumes blend well with their surroundings and give the buildings an identity.

position.rationale: The two-part composition and differing heights are directly visible in the calibrated renders.

positive.statement: The library views, daylight and transparency are exciting.

position.rationale: Library interior is not identifiable; the prominent taller wing is the likely location.

positive.statement: The sports facilities are well arranged and their room program is complete and very well organized.

position.rationale: The low-level western portion is used as the likely partly underground sports zone.

positive.statement: The compactness and limited number of structures provide prerequisites for high cost-effectiveness and low energy consumption.

position.rationale: Cost and energy performance have no useful spatial referent.

negative.statement: The enclosed outdoor areas cannot convey the desired open-space atmosphere or direct contact with the natural terrain.

position.rationale: The courtyard and enclosed spaces between the two volumes are clearly visible in plan and low elevations.

negative.statement: The main entrance lacks the desired significance at its proposed location.

position.rationale: The square-facing edge of the taller building provides a directional entrance anchor.

negative.statement: The proposed alternatives to the planned park routing and elements are not convincing.

position.rationale: Park context is represented by the open area around the compact masses, without explicit route geometry.

negative.statement: The underground gymnasium contributes little to social control of the playground in the evenings and at weekends.

position.rationale: The low western mass is consistent with the partly underground gymnasium location.

negative.statement: The basic level is in the most public area, but its building depth prevents direct connections to associated outdoor spaces.

position.rationale: The lower, square-facing portion of the taller building is used as the public-level anchor.

negative.statement: In the second stage, the inner courtyard loses much of its quality and daylight.

position.rationale: The central gap between masses provides the identifiable courtyard anchor.

negative.statement: Daycare-center room allocation is only partly successful, with complicated access, confined spaces and poorly visible niches.

position.rationale: Daycare rooms are interior; the taller eastern wing is a constrained surface approximation.

negative.statement: The intervention in the historic building causes a major loss of substance and is not approvable in this form.

position.rationale: The western volume is used as an approximate location for the historic-building intervention.

negative.statement: The school building over the gymnasium creates high shear stresses requiring correspondingly dimensioned beams.

position.rationale: The stacked low western portion indicates the building-over-gymnasium condition.
